title: Add sccache-backed warm builds without placeholder checksums
summary: Retry of the failed sccache change: jobs keep their own CARGO_TARGET_DIR (isolation) but compile through a shared content-addressed sccache. The pinned sccache is installed by setup in a way that needs no hand-copied digests, so setup and builds cannot be broken by fake values.

defaults_applied.how: Use the maintained sccache crate rather than building a cache; record the call.
No claim of provenance for values that were not measured; cite the cold-build timing from the request.
Config tests enforce wrapper/version match and cargo test and clippy pass.
Tests enforce the sccache wiring and reject placeholder digests rather than relying on comments.
One focused change to build wiring and its decision record.
Decision and changelog written for an outside reader.

assumptions: The producer cannot download release assets to learn real sha256 values, so it must not write any digest it did not measure; an all-zero or invented digest is forbidden.

sccache is installed by setup with `cargo install sccache --locked --version <pin> --root <athena_home>/tools/sccache/<pin>`, whose crate downloads are checksum-verified by crates.io/Cargo.lock-style verification, instead of a release tarball with a sha256 table. If the owner prefers release tarballs, they must supply real digests.
RUSTC_WRAPPER in the change and study capability environments points at the installed binary, and setup installs it before any job can run, so the wrapper never names a missing program.
The shared cache directory (SCCACHE_DIR) lives under athena_home, outside any job directory, and is keyed by content, so job isolation of target dirs (D46) is kept.
A new decision (D79) supersedes the part of D46 that left out sccache, and records the cold-build evidence (~165s test check).
question: Should sccache be installed with `cargo install --locked` (no digest needed, slower first setup), or from release tarballs for which you will supply the real sha256 values?

acceptance_criteria.text: athena.toml contains no all-zero or placeholder digest, and no claim in athena.toml, CHANGELOG.md or docs/decisions.md says a value was copied from upstream unless it was.
CARGO_TARGET_DIR stays per job and per side in [capabilities.change.env] and [capabilities.study.env]; RUSTC_WRAPPER and SCCACHE_DIR are added there, with SCCACHE_DIR outside the job directory.

setup.sh (or the setup code in xtask) installs the pinned sccache version before it builds Athena, and fails clearly if the install fails; the version is defined once and the wrapper path is derived from or tested against it.
docs/decisions.md records a new decision with alternatives and the tradeoff, and marks D46's sccache exclusion as superseded; CHANGELOG.md has an entry.
A config test asserts the change and study environments set RUSTC_WRAPPER to the pinned sccache path and keep CARGO_TARGET_DIR per job; run `cargo test --locked` and it passes.
If any digest table is kept, a test rejects all-zero digests; `cargo test --locked` passes.

out_of_scope: Sharing CARGO_TARGET_DIR across jobs or sides.
Changing check commands, gitleaks pin, or CI workflows.
departures: Cost and time raised: the prior attempt failed, the change touches setup and config, and a new tool install may lengthen cold checks. Pass rate lowered because the real tool cannot be exercised by the verifier's allowed commands.
